svg.title: Step 7 mockup 25: Clips and photos from anyone taking part: links or files, approved by the crew, all kept
svg.text: 25 · Clips and photos from anyone taking part: links or files, approved by the crew, all kept
Use case: players share game footage and photos by a link or a file; the crew approves; only approved items reach the screen; everything is kept for the LAN video. No consent steps. Demo names only.

Choose a file, or drop it on a PC

The platform tries to save a copy of a link when it is sent, from hosts the event trusts, within a size,
type and time limit. A Steam link expires: if the copy fails, the sender is asked for the file. The
link stays in the export list, never shown on the screen. Any other link: the page says it is not
Three places an approved item can show
In its recap, right after the
In the lead-up: the best of
• Each approved item shows at most 3 times an hour (a setting).
• Newest and least-shown first, spread fairly across players.
• The crew can pin one or push one now.
• Clips play muted for about 30 s at most, unless the crew allows sound.
on the queue row, by the crew
7 · One export per event, for the LAN video: every file and a list of the links
Shown or not, every clip and photo is in the export.
Game captures are game footage: no consent step and no removal flow. Tagging is optional. The crew
queue is the only gate, and the crew can delete an item.
A participant sends a file or a link (YouTube, Twitch, Medal, Steam); the platform tries to save a copy,
and the crew approves it like an upload.
Crew uploads skip the queue; a participant's item never does. Files sit in the files volume with a size
Showing is capped and fair: a few times an hour, newest and least-shown first, spread across players.
